description: A feature flag read inside the ad service's `GetAds` handler activated a singleton `CPULoad` that spawned 4 daemon threads each running a tight `Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis())` loop; the threads pinned CPU cores and saturated container CPU and `jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio` on the `ad` service.
mechanism: The flag is read in [`AdService.java#L172`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/AdService.java#L172): on every `getAds` gRPC call, `CPULoad.getInstance().execute()` is invoked with the boolean value of the `adHighCpu` flag. When the flag is `true`, [`CPULoad.java#L46-L52`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L46) calls `spawnLoadWorkers(4)`, which launches 4 daemon threads ([`CPULoad.java#L64-L74`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L64)). Each thread runs a tight `while(shouldRun) { Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()); }` loop ([`CPULoad.java#L101-L103`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L101)), saturating CPU cores with continuous logarithm calculations. The threads persist until the flag is toggled off, at which point `stopWorkers()` sets `shouldRun=false` on each thread. Because the workers are spawned only once (guarded by the `running` flag at line 49), repeated `getAds` calls while the flag is on do not create additional threads.

variants.description: CPU utilization of the ad container spiked from ~0.2 to ~400 (~4 full cores) because the adHighCpu flag spawned 4 daemon threads running tight Math.log() loops that saturate CPU
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~0.17–0.28. At 16:36 the value jumps to ~401.9, a ~2000x increase, clearly the first timestamp where the spike begins.

variants.description: JVM CPU utilization ratio for the ad service jumped from ~0.03% to ~49%, directly caused by the 4 Logarithmizer daemon threads running tight Math.log() loops that saturate CPU cores.
variants.onset_reasoning: The metric is 0 at 16:52, then jumps to ~0.49 at 16:53, clearly spiking above the zero baseline. This is the first timestamp showing the spike after the incident time.

variants.description: Host-level idle CPU utilization collapsed from ~95% to ~45% as the ad service's CPU-saturating threads consumed available idle CPU capacity
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident, the metric oscillates around 0.94-0.96 (CPU idle ratio). At 16:36 the value is 0.951621, still within the normal range. At 16:37 it drops sharply to 0.444737 and stays flat around 0.44-0.47 thereafter, indicating a collapse in CPU idle time (i.e., heavy CPU usage). The last timestamp showing the pre-incident active pattern is 16:36, making it the onset of the collapse.

variants.description: The flagd impression counter for adHighCpu with variant 'on' increased from 5 to 7 (rate went from 0 to non-zero) after the flag was toggled, recording that flagd evaluated the adHighCpu feature flag as enabled.
variants.onset_reasoning: The metric is flat at 0 through 16:35 (incident time). At 16:36 it jumps to ~0.00417, which is the first non-zero value after the incident, indicating the adHighCpu feature flag 'on' variant began being evaluated. This is the clear onset of the spike.

variants.description: Rate of JVM CPU time consumption for the ad service spiked from ~0.002 to ~3.8 seconds/second, reflecting the 4 CPU-bound daemon threads continuously consuming CPU cycles.
variants.onset_reasoning: With only two data points, both after the incident time, the first timestamp (16:53:00) at 1.8565 already shows an elevated value consistent with a CPU spike beginning. The subsequent point at 16:54:00 (2.5882) confirms the upward trend. The onset is the first available data point showing the spike.

logs.name: ad: High CPU-Load problempattern enabled (INFO)
logs.description: At 16:35:10.466 UTC, the ad service emitted 17 INFO logs announcing that the High CPU-Load problem pattern had been enabled.
logs.cause: Smoking-gun direct evidence of the adHighCpu flag. On every getAds invocation, AdService.java:172 calls ffClient.getBooleanValue("adHighCpu", false, ctx) and passes the result to CPULoad.execute(enabled). When enabled=true, CPULoad.java:48 logs "High CPU-Load problempattern enabled" at INFO and, if not already running, spawns 4 daemon Logarithmizer threads (CPULoad.java:50, 64-73) that tight-loop Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()) to saturate CPU. Note the log is not an error — the ad service continues serving requests successfully, just under CPU pressure.
logs.source: ad service (Java, oteldemo.problempattern.CPULoad logger via OpenTelemetry Java agent)
